title: Probation Success Bucket and Mentor Rotation Protocol
body:
Purpose:
Provide a lightweight, reproducible protocol to (1) define a small set of "success buckets" that constitute passing probation for IC roles and (2) run an intentional mentor rotation to reduce single-person onboarding risk. This is a pragmatic playbook for people-ops + hiring managers to use when designing 30/60/90s and calibrating offers.

Context and motivation:
- Observed pain: uneven probation outcomes driven by inconsistent expectations and single-mentor bottlenecks.
- Goal: standardize pass criteria across similar role families, make evidence explicit, and create a repeatable mentor-rotation handoff so new hires get a diversity of signals and feedback.
- Scope: IC engineers (backend/frontend/infra), product managers, and solutions engineers. Leadership roles follow a separate calibration path.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Create 3–5 role-specific "success buckets" (technical delivery, collaboration + communication, operational ownership, learning velocity).
- Each bucket has 2–4 observable signals (tickets shipped, PR quality, triage leadership, docs owned, bugs reduced).
- Assign 2 mentors + a peer buddy. Rotate mentors every 2 weeks for the first 8 weeks. Handoff checklist must be filled at rotation.
- Use an "evidence ledger" (shared doc) where mentors and the hire log 1–3 artifacts per week tied to buckets.

Success buckets (example template) — keep short and measurable:
1) Technical delivery (outcome, not hours)
   - Signals: at least 1 small production change merged (owner-level), code review comments addressed within SLA, a deterministic test added for a regression class.
2) Collaboration & communication
   - Signals: runs a short async update in team channel, leads one pairing session, stakeholder sync scheduled + notes posted.
3) Operational ownership
   - Signals: owns one oncall rotation task or runbook update, reduces a recurring alert by a measurable amount, postmortem contributor.
4) Learning velocity & feedback loop
   - Signals: weekly learning goals recorded, evidence ledger contains progress artifacts, implements feedback from mentor within 1 cycle.

Rubric guidance (quick):
- For each bucket, score on 1–5 scale. Passing threshold: majority of buckets >= 3 and no bucket <= 2 if that bucket is core to role.
- Use comments to tie score to artifacts (link to PR, doc, ticket). Avoid vague language.

Mentor rotation protocol (operational):
- Roles: Primary mentor (first 2 weeks), Secondary mentor (weeks 3–4), Cross-domain mentor (weeks 5–8), Peer buddy (ongoing).
- Cadence: 30–45 min mentor sync twice weekly for first 4 weeks, then weekly through week 8. Peer buddy meets 2x/week for ramp tasks.
- Rotation: switch primary mentor responsibility every 2 weeks for 8 weeks (so hire sees 3 distinct mentors total). Purpose is breadth of perspective and reduced single-point-of-failure.
- Handoff checklist (required at rotation):
   * List of open tickets owned by hire + status (Jira keys)
   * Short notes on learning blockers (2 bullets max)
   * Outstanding PRs and reviewers needed
   * One suggested micro-scope for next 2 weeks (<= 3d work)
   * Evidence ledger pointer (link) + one artifact to review
- Handoff must be completed in writing before mentor change; incoming mentor schedules a 30m sync to align.

Evidence ledger (how we record):
- Single shared doc per hire (template attached in GITHUB link above). Headers: week, bucket, artifact type (PR/Doc/Ticket/Runbook), link, short note, mentor sign-off.
- Minimum: 1 artifact/week for first 8 weeks; 2/week preferred for delivery roles.

Interview/hire plan tie-ins (to reduce probation risk):
- When hiring, capture 2+ signals that map to success buckets (e.g., take-home that exercises ownership, behavioral question about cross-team tradeoffs).
- Interview rubric should include explicit items for "mentorship dose" (how the candidate learns from peers) and "handoff mindset" (can they document and handoff a task?).
- For marginal hires, consider a structured 6-month ramp with checkpointed re-evaluation at 60 days (not just 90).

Onboarding checklist (first 30/60/90 highlights) — actionable items to attach to evidence ledger:
- Day 0–7: account accesses, dev env green, first pairing session scheduled, review of team's incident runbook.
- Week 2: small production change deployed with mentor; first evidence ledger entry.
- Week 4: owns a small triage or customer ask end-to-end.
- Week 8: leads an internal demo or doc update; mentor rotation complete.
- Week 12: cross-functional stakeholder feedback captured and added to ledger.

Managers: calibration & check-ins
- Weekly manager sync should review ledger artifacts (5–10 min). Formal manager checkpoint at day 30 and day 60 (15–30 min) and probation review at day 90.
- If manager observes 2 consecutive weeks with no artifacts, escalate to people-ops to diagnose.

Escalation triggers (examples)
- Missed two rotation handoffs in a row without written notes.
- Zero artifacts logged in ledger after week 3.
- Clear safety/regulatory concern.

Templates & tooling (short)
- Evidence ledger template: GITHUB:company/onboarding-templates/pull/58 (linked above).
- JIRA labels: onboarding:<hire-name>, onboarding:artifact. Add label to any ticket that counts as evidence.
- Confluence page: HR/Probation-Framework-2025 — canonical definitions and legal considerations.

Open questions / TODOs (work in progress)
- How to scale mentor rotations for very small teams (1–2 engineers)? Proposal: cross-pod mentor pairings with neighboring team. Need budget signal.
- Should manager have veto power to extend probation by 30 days automatically? Legal review required. (JIRA:HR-4123)
- Add direct manager training for running written handoffs — short async module needed.

Notes to self / pragmatics:
- Keep buckets intentionally small to avoid "checkboxing" — we want narratives tied to artifacts.
- Save a few anonymized case studies of successful rotations for an internal playbook page.
- Align with Legal on language for extension and evidence retention.

References and links:
- Confluence: HR/Probation-Framework-2025 (policy + legal guidance)
- JIRA: HR-4123 (policy questions thread)
- GitHub: onboarding-templates PR with ledger template

If you're reviewing this: please add suggestions inline. Next step: pilot with two hires in Q1 and collect metrics (percent passing at 90 days, average artifacts/week, mentor satisfaction score).
